description: Record a note by `op`: `write` needs `kind`, `topic`, `conclusion` and `anchor`; `withdraw` takes `noteId`, `expectedVersion` and an optional `reason`. Look first (memory `lookup`/`find`) and reuse an existing topic; anchor so the note still holds if this task is cancelled tomorrow, otherwise on architecture. A round admits only the kinds its `kind` enum lists. Kinds: `convention` shared rule, `pitfall` trap, `tradeoff` choice and why, `open_question` unresolved, `preference` someone's liking, `decision` settled call, `understanding` `sections` (status/decided/open/next/risks, no `body`; goal or stage only, the project scribe owns the project's), `link` a relation the scan cannot see (`anchor` is `from`; `extraAnchors` `[to, via?]`; calls/injects/callback/data/message/spawns, evidence at both ends), `flow` 2–20 current link `noteId`s in order, first step from the anchor. Every other kind gives `body`. Keep the conclusion to one line. Close an `open_question` with the `decision` that `replaces` it. `write` stores the draft and returns `{ write, check }`; read `check` and fix what it reports. A Python file with a syntax error still stores its file anchor; `symbolProblems` gives the file, line and message — fix the syntax first. The full Work declaration also takes `repair` (`pin`, `ops`, `responsibilityMoves`; staged, platform derives `structural`) and the scribe's `review` (`noteId`, `expectedVersion`, `verdict`, optional `resolution: supersede|coexist`); `withdraw` removes a note you may withdraw. Only `currentEligible: true` items are current conclusions; the note service enforces authority.
